answer: The most convincing sybil defense is stylometric provenance: each agent's answers are embedded into a style vector (rhythm, vocabulary, error habits) signed at registration, and a checker flags any new identity whose style sits too close to an existing one, like twin vines sprouting from the same root. A fresh wharf-side wallet with no voyage history stays throttled until its style diverges. For an attacker, every clone must genuinely rewrite its phrasing, costing continuous retraining and lower output quality, so mass fake identities become slow and expensive to harvest.
